newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-Australia's Evans says services lightly taxed.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-Australia's Evans says services lightly taxed.

text.p: Australian Treasury Secretary Ted Evans said on Monday that the country's services sector was rapidly growing into a major sector of the economy and was lightly taxed.
"Services continue to grow and continued to be lightly taxed," Evans told a luncheon of business economists in Sydney.
He had been asked if the tax base needed to be broadened through the introduction a consumption tax.

The current conservative Liberal-National coalition government has said it would not introduce a goods and services (GST) consumption tax in its current three year parliamentary term which expires in 1999.
But it has not ruled out a GST in future terms if it was re-elected.
The coalition campaigned for a GST before the 1993 election, which it lost against expectations, due, some have said, to its plans for a GST.
Various business groups and even some social welfare groups have recently called for the introduction of a GST to broaden the tax base to make it easier for government to fund its spending.
Opinion polls also show a GST coming back into favour, with a recent opinion poll showing more people support its introduction than oppose it.
Outgoing Reserve Bank of Australia Governor Bernie Fraser said last month the introduction of a GST would come back onto the government's agenda.
